title: test-0108-MAT-NUMBERS6
passage: In the Indian numbering system, we use commas to separate periods of ones, thousands, and lakhs. For example, the number 1,234,567 is written as 12,34,567 because the first comma is after three digits, but subsequent commas appear after every two digits. Understanding place value is crucial; the digit 5 in 12,34,567 represents 500 because it sits in the hundreds place, not just the value 5. When we round numbers to the nearest ten, we look at the digit in the ones place. If that digit is 5 or greater, we round up to the next ten. For instance, 45 rounds up to 50, not down to 40. Finally, Roman numerals follow strict rules. Symbols like I, X, and C can be repeated up to three times, but never four times. Therefore, the number 40 is written as XL, not XXXX, because we subtract 10 from 50. Comparing numbers is also simple: a number with more digits is always greater than one with fewer digits, but if the digit count is equal, we compare from the leftmost place. A number like 005 is just 5, so it is smaller than 12.
